Subject: PO vs Card — Procurement next steps / FinTechCo

Hi Elena / Marco —

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the time. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can move from discovery into procurement: 

What we heard
- Primary use case: customer-facing personalization at scale (inference-heavy)
- Target go-live: Q4 pilot, production H1 2027
- Key procurement constraints: AP prefers marketplace purchases when possible; larger deals require PO + vendor onboarding + W-9; smaller/one-off purchases often go on corporate P-card

Commercial options we discussed
- Option A (recommended for predictable capacity): Reserved capacity with monthly invoice via PO (Net30 subject to credit approval)
- Option B: Self-service on card for pilots/smaller spend; also possible via AWS Marketplace if you want consolidated procurement controls

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm whether FinTechCo will need a signed MSA and a PO for the initial commit?
2) Please share the procurement contact (name/email) and any vendor onboarding form or required docs (W-9, bank info, compliance questionnaire) — I copied Dylan and Laura to help with vendor onboarding and technical setup.
3) Attached is a preliminary quote for the scope we discussed. If PO is the path, we can issue an invoice and attach the MSA. If you prefer marketplace, we can list the offer there (it typically shortens vendor onboarding).

Attachments: [attachment: Quote-Redwood-PO-20260627.pdf (PDF, 12KB)]

Happy to schedule a 20-min follow-up with Marco + procurement to walk through vendor onboarding. What works for you next week?

Thanks,

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from procurement side: 

- For anything expected to exceed $50k annually we do require a PO and vendor onboarding. Smaller pilots that stay under that threshold can usually be done on P-card.
- Our AP team prefers marketplace purchases (AWS Marketplace) where possible because it ties into our spend controls; however, not all vendors are available there and listing can take a couple of weeks to finalize.
- For vendor onboarding we will need a W-9 (for US vendors), a completed vendor setup form, and our legal team may ask for the MSA redline.

I've looped in Marco Bianchi (procurement lead) who will own the vendor onboarding. Marco — can you confirm timeline for onboarding and whether we can proceed via marketplace or need a direct PO?

Also, can Redwood provide a TIN and bank wiring instructions if needed? And are Net30 terms an option?

Best,
Elena Rossi
Director of Finance Operations | FinTechCo
elena.rossi@fintechco.com
